chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Tariq, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the woman reaches fifty years, she does not see red (blood) unless she is a woman from Quraish.

key_terms.خَمْسِينَ سَنَةً: Fifty years, the specified age for menopause
key_terms.قُرَيْشٍ: Quraish, the tribe of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), mentioned here as an exception

ai.seo_question: At what age does a woman's menstruation cease according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the age of fifty as the standard limit for menopause (ya's al-haydh) in Shia jurisprudence, while noting an exception for women of the Quraysh tribe whose menstruation may persist longer. This ruling is foundational for determining when a woman transitions from the category of 'baligh' (menstruating) to 'mu'annaqa' (elderly non-menstruating), which impacts her ritual purity obligations and marital status. The specific mention of Quraysh reflects historical observations of lineage-based physiological variations recognized by early scholars.
